common_affordance: The combination of incidence-form candidate vectors and the span requirement invites reduction to graph connectivity, after which the survivors incorrectly replace the minimum shared Steiner subgraph by an MST on pairwise terminal shortest-path distances.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It applies an MST/Kruskal-style connection directly to the target vertices and does not correctly account for intermediate Steiner vertices or shared edges.

recommended_edit: Add an explicit clarification immediately after the definition of W: "A selected candidate is paid for only once and may simultaneously contribute to connecting multiple target indices. Intermediate non-target indices may be shared by those connections, so independently choosing shortest paths between target pairs is not valid; the required optimization is over the minimum-cost shared connecting subgraph."
regression_risk: This clarification could help a model that was previously defeated by the ambiguity recognize the Steiner-tree formulation and start solving correctly.
